subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What private-session contract should OpenClaw expose and enforce for this issue: a full no-read/no-write/no-history mode, a narrower demo-only context suppression mode, or no core private mode for now?
rationale: This feature creates a user-facing privacy promise and new protocol/config/UI behavior; automation cannot safely choose the threat model or persistence boundaries without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design full private-session contract
options.body: Define and then implement an additive private/ephemeral session bit that every transcript, memory, compaction, plugin, channel, tool/artifact, and UI path must honor before promising privacy.

options.title: Narrow to demo-only context suppression
options.body: Limit the first version to stock-persona/no-bootstrap context for screen sharing, and avoid claiming no-persistence until the durable enforcement work is separately designed.

options.title: Defer core private mode
options.body: Keep existing contextInjection and session cleanup as the supported mitigations, leaving this issue open or closing only after maintainers decide the broader privacy promise is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design full private-session contract
recommendation.body: Define and then implement an additive private/ephemeral session bit that every transcript, memory, compaction, plugin, channel, tool/artifact, and UI path must honor before promising privacy.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the prior canonical keep-open review and framed the missing cross-surface privacy contract that maintainers need to decide.
